subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should this issue be split so the open schedule-activation PR owns stale replay, while maintainers separately define cron delete and emergency outbound-stop semantics?
rationale: Current main has partial interrupted-run and cancellation machinery, but the issue asks for both a persisted replay boundary and a user-facing guarantee for stopping active outbound sends.

options.title: Split Replay And Emergency Stop
options.body: Review or replace the schedule-activation PR for stale replay, and keep this issue as the product anchor for delete/emergency-stop semantics.

options.title: Single Combined Fix
options.body: Require one coordinated PR to address replay, delete cancellation, and outbound halt behavior before closing this issue.

options.title: Replay Only
options.body: Treat emergency stop as out of scope and close only after restart catch-up is fixed, accepting a narrower result.

recommendation.title: Split Replay And Emergency Stop
recommendation.body: Review or replace the schedule-activation PR for stale replay, and keep this issue as the product anchor for delete/emergency-stop semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest history signal for the startup catch-up split and adjacent cron restart behavior.
